articles.title: Extreme heat on Independence Day will be America's new normal, experts say
articles.description: In cities across the U.S., parades were canceled and events were delayed because of the heat. Meanwhile, emergency rooms saw a high number of people with heat-related illnesses.

articles.title: China test-launches ballistic missile from sub in South Pacific, draws protests
articles.description: China's military test-launched a long-range ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine in the South Pacific, drawing protest and concern from countries in the region.

articles.title: Balogun's red card suspension lifted after Trump called FIFA chief
articles.description: Balogun's reinstatement came after President Trump called FIFA President Gianni Infantino last week and asked for a review of the red card suspension.

articles.title: FIFA criticized for lifting U.S. star's red card suspension after Trump phone call
articles.description: Europe's soccer governing body and prominent commentators have criticized the decision, which allows Folarin Balogun to play against Belgium.

articles.title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup schedule and how to watch
articles.description: With 104 World Cup games being played in the U.S., Canada and Mexico, it's like "a Super Bowl every single day for five weeks," U.S. team captain Tim Ream told CBS News.

articles.title: This World Cup marks end of era for Ronaldo and other soccer greats
articles.description: Some of the greatest footballers of a generation played their final World Cup match this summer.

articles.title: USA set to take on Belgium in World Cup amid Trump red card controversy
articles.description: Ahead of this evening's World Cup match between the U.S. and Belgium, the drama about the eligibility of U.S. striker Folarin Balogun continues to swirl following his red card in the previous match.

articles.title: Supreme Court lets Texas restrict minors' access to app stores for the time being
articles.description: Texas' App Store Accountability Act requires minors to have their parents' permission to download most apps. The Supreme Court says the law can go into effect as lawsuits continue in lower courts.

articles.title: Graham Platner faces growing calls to withdraw following allegation of sexual assault
articles.description: The Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine said he was assessing next steps after allegations of sexual assault were reported on Monday by Politico. Platner denied them as "categorically untrue."

articles.title: Trump says U.S. will win war "one way or the other" as Iran holds Khamenei's funeral
articles.description: The U.S. is "going to win one way or the other," Trump said Monday, as Iran held a colossal public funeral for their slain supreme leader.

articles.title: Kyiv apartment building hit by multiple Russian strikes month apart
articles.description: Residents of a Kyiv apartment building hit a second time by a Russian strike greeted emergency responders with dark humor, volunteer Kateryna Tereshkova said.

articles.title: Man confesses from jail to killing wife, says he will reveal location of body
articles.description: Delphine Jubillar went missing in southern France in December 2020 at the height of the COVID pandemic and her body was never found.

articles.title: Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine's capital kills at least 22
articles.description: All the ballistic missiles launched by Russia struck their targets, underscoring Kyiv's need for more U.S. Patriot interceptor missiles, Ukraine officials say.

articles.title: Man sues DHS after agents tracked him down for sending a scathing email to ICE
articles.description: Federal agents tried to track David Streever to his home and hotel, and left him a warning notice that a critical email he sent the former head of ICE may have been illegal. Now he's suing.

articles.title: Super Typhoon Bavi makes landfall near Guam with extreme, life-threatening winds
articles.description: Bavi, a massive cyclone approaching the Mariana Islands east of the Philippines, was forecast to strike Rota early Monday morning local time.

articles.title: Militant LGBTQ+ rights group 'the Lavender Panthers' was founded on this day in 1973
articles.description: "Reverend Ray" Broshears founded the queer vigilante group the Lavender Panthers in 1973. The group's impact is still felt today.

articles.title: Historic World Cup furor at 'incomprehensible' FIFA decision to let U.S. forward Balogun play
articles.description: The Belgian soccer federation is challenging FIFA's ruling to let Balogun play despite getting a red card in his previous game. Belgium's statement came just 11 hours before kickoff in Seattle. European soccer body UEFA criticizes FIFA's "incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision."

articles.title: EasyJet agrees to $6.7 billion takeover by U.S. private equity firm
articles.description: U.K. budget airline has struck a deal to be acquired after rejecting four previous offers by the American investment firm.

articles.title: Iran begins funeral procession for slain supreme leader
articles.description: Mourners poured into the streets of Tehran for the funeral procession of Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. He was killed in an airstrike at the beginning of the war with the U.S and Israel. Ramy Inocencio reports.

articles.title: Prince Harry at odds with Buckingham Palace over U.K. stay
articles.description: Prince's Harry's spokesperson says an offer to stay was "withdrawn at the last moment," which the Palace denies
